title: Choose the visual world for your portfolio
question: The roll assigned Component Datasheet. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Component Datasheet
options.lineage: semiconductor datasheets and engineering spec sheets
options.thesis: Your CV published as the spec sheet of a part: features, ratings, block diagram, timing diagram, ordering information.
options.viewport: A cobalt cover sheet: your name at poster scale, a features column with the CV's real figures, and a live block diagram where signals run from iOS, Android and Flutter through to the shipped apps. 'Download datasheet' is the CV; 'Request a sample' is email.
options.risk: Can read as a gimmick if the jargon outruns the content; every label needs a plain-English twin.

raised.raise: Figures are set at poster scale and are the interface themselves; no card chrome around a number.
The sheet's ground changes in whole bands as you scroll, cobalt cover to pale paper to ink close, as one continuous transition.
Every diagram develops in a fixed order: keyline first, then values, then the moving signal.
Each infographic is a numbered figure with a ruled caption at its foot, so the page reads as one catalogued system.

options.label: Store Listing
options.lineage: App Store and Google Play product pages
options.thesis: You, presented as an app listing: icon, fact strip, preview panels, version history as career, information table.
options.viewport: App-icon monogram, name and title, a 'Contact' pill where 'Get' sits, then the familiar fact strip: 4M+ users, 12+ micro-apps, 60+ screens, 5+ years.
options.risk: Also the direction many mobile-developer portfolios land on, and it wants real screenshots you don't have.

options.label: Typographic Tiles
options.lineage: Metro design language: flat tiles and giant lowercase
options.thesis: No chrome at all: giant lowercase words and flat colour tiles that flip to show your figures.
options.viewport: 'hosam elnabawy' in giant light lowercase running off the right edge, over a grid of flat tiles: a wide '4m+ users' tile, live tiles flipping between projects.
options.case: Holds on clarity: tiles carry numbers well. Loses on identification: a phone design language you never shipped for.
options.risk: Reads as a period piece from a platform outside your CV.

options.label: Cyclorama Dawn
options.thesis: Career as a lighting cue sequence from night to day.
options.viewport: A black field with a cobalt horizon band rising behind your name.
options.case: Atmosphere without evidence: recruiters need figures, not a mood.
options.kept: One continuous ground transition across the scroll.

options.label: Darkroom Safelight
options.thesis: Projects develop like prints under amber light.
options.viewport: An amber field where your name emerges from a developer tray.
options.case: Slow reveal fights a reader who has one minute.
options.kept: Diagrams that develop in a fixed, staged order.
options.risk: Hides the content behind the effect.

options.label: Ornament Plate Book
options.thesis: Skills as repeatable ornament units on numbered plates.
options.viewport: A numbered plate of interlaced units with your name in a constructed alphabet.
options.case: The parts-catalogue idea fits a design system, but the ornament says craft guild, not mobile engineering.

options.label: Fluid Ink Basin
options.thesis: The page as a liquid surface the pointer stirs.
options.viewport: A white basin of indigo ink with your name in the margin.
options.case: A GPU toy says nothing about scale or seniority.
options.kept: Diagrams that answer the pointer continuously.

options.label: Industrial Quote Grammar
options.thesis: Every section labelled in quoted caps with hazard stripes.
options.viewport: "ENGINEER" in giant quoted caps over a hazard stripe.
options.case: Fashion irony undercuts the professionalism you asked for.
options.risk: Reads as a joke to a hiring manager.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: The dark developer portfolio: centred hero, gradient accents, cards for projects and skills, executed cleanly.
canonCard.viewport: Name and title centred on a dark ground with two buttons and a stat row beneath.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from most developer portfolios by design.
